---
title: "How do I calculate the probability of A given that B occurred?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I calculate the probability of A given that B occurred?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Identify event B (given) and count its occurrences.

2. Count observations where both A and B hold.

3. Divide the joint count by the B count.

## Runnable example

```{r}
rain <- c(TRUE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,TRUE)
wind <- c(TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE)
denom <- sum(rain)
if (denom==0L) stop("No observations satisfy the given event.")
p <- sum(wind & rain)/denom
print(c(joint=sum(wind & rain),given=denom,conditional=p))
```

## Interpret the result

Wind occurred on three of the five sampled rainy days. The observed probability of wind given rain is 3/5, or 0.6.

## Check before using your own data

If no observations satisfy B, the conditional sample proportion is undefined. Keep the denominator explicit.
